criteria_results.title: Caption includes correct case number
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion captions repeatedly list the Civil Action No. as 2:24-cv-00831-CAR, which matches the required case number.

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies correct court
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion caption expressly identifies the court as the United States District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania.

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies Vantage Industrial Holdings, Inc. as Plaintiff
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption names “VANTAGE INDUSTRIAL HOLDINGS, INC.” and identifies it as “Plaintiff.”

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies Corbin Machining & Fabrication, LLC as Defendant
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption repeatedly names “CORBIN MACHINING & FABRICATION, LLC” and identifies it as “Defendant.”

criteria_results.title: Motion directed to Magistrate Judge Sheehan
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly references Magistrate Judge David P. Sheehan, invokes his Standing Order regarding discovery motions, includes the required summary chart pursuant to that order, and the proposed order is directed for signature by Magistrate Judge Sheehan. Although the caption also lists District Judge Radford, the discovery motion is presented to Magistrate Judge Sheehan for resolution.

criteria_results.title: Motion identifies Rule 37(a) as statutory basis
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion explicitly cites Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 37(a) in the title and opening paragraph as a basis for the motion to compel.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Argues failure to produce privilege log
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues that Corbin asserted attorney-client privilege and work-product objections, including for RFP No. 14 and other requests, but failed to serve a privilege log required by Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(5)(A) and the CMO. It seeks waiver or an order compelling a compliant log.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Cites Rule 26(b)(5)(A) for privilege log requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly states that Corbin withheld documents without a privilege log “in violation of Rule 26(b)(5)(A),” and the memorandum’s privilege-log argument quotes and cites Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(5)(A) as requiring a party asserting privilege to make the claim and describe withheld documents.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Argues privilege waiver for failure to produce log
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues that Corbin failed to serve a privilege log required by Rule 26(b)(5)(A) and the CMO, states the log was overdue, and asks the Court to deem attorney-client privilege and work-product objections waived on that basis. The proposed order also includes a waiver finding tied to the missing log.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Notes broken promise to produce privilege log
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly references the broken privilege-log promise: it states that Corbin’s counsel conceded the omission during the August 28 meet-and-confer, promised a log within approximately 30 days/by September 28, 2024, and still had not served one. The Local Rule 37.1 certification identifies Lauren Ybarra as Corbin’s counsel on that call and states the log was never produced as of the October 15 filing, after the October 14 deadline.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Challenges boilerplate overbreadth objections
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly challenges Corbin’s general and boilerplate objections, including overbreadth objections, as improper under Rules 33 and 34 and the CMO. It argues that Corbin’s overbreadth/burden/proportionality objections are unsupported by declarations, estimates, or specific factual showings, cites Josephs for the insufficiency of conclusory objections, and asks the court to overrule/strike them.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: States objecting party bears burden of justification
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly states in the Legal Standard that after the movant shows relevance, “the burden then shifts to the objecting party to show specifically why discovery should not be had,” and elsewhere argues Corbin must support burden/proportionality and trade-secret objections with specific evidence. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Challenges trade secret objection to RFP No. 5
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically identifies RFP No. 5 as seeking QC records, inspection reports, CMM/metallurgical data, etc., notes Corbin objected on trade secret grounds, and argues that the trade-secret claim is unsupported, improper without a Rule 26(c) protective-order motion, and should be overruled or handled through a protective order.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Argues trade secret claim requires protective order motion
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues that trade-secret/confidentiality concerns must be addressed through a Rule 26(c) protective order and notes that Corbin never filed a protective-order motion as required by the CMO. It also states that bare trade-secret objections are unsupported and should be overruled.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Notes Corbin failed to identify specific trade secrets
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues that Corbin’s trade-secret claim was unsupported and non-specific, noting the CMO required Corbin to identify the specific information claimed as a trade secret and that Corbin “has done none of this.” It applies this point to quality-control materials such as the quality manual, SOPs, CMM data, metallurgical results, and related records.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies Interrogatory No. 18 as evasive
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically discusses Interrogatory No. 18 and says Corbin’s answer is contradicted by CORBIN-000247 and seeks a complete, truthful supplemental answer. However, it does not specifically identify the Interrogatory No. 18 response as “evasive” or “incomplete” under Rule 37(a)(4); Rule 37(a)(4) is applied elsewhere to other responses, not to No. 18.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Uses Foss email to impeach Interrogatory No. 18 response
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly cites the September 14, 2022 Gerald Foss email to Raymond Corbin (CORBIN-000247), quoting that 15 housings failed CMM inspection but were cleared for shipment per Corbin's instruction, and expressly argues that this contradicts Corbin's verified response to Interrogatory No. 18 claiming no awareness of failed parts shipped to Vantage.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies Foss email as inadvertently produced
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly indicates that the Foss email came from Corbin’s own production, including by identifying it as “Corbin’s own document CORBIN-000247,” stating that Corbin’s 312-page production included “the Foss email,” and citing the Bates number CORBIN-000247 throughout.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Addresses missing Certificates of Conformance
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion explicitly states that Corbin produced CoCs for only 12 of 47 purchase orders and claims the remaining 35 cannot be located after a diligent search, and it seeks relief regarding the search, retention policies, and a sworn declaration.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Cites MSA seven-year retention requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly cites MSA § 9.4 as requiring Corbin to retain Quality Records/CoCs for seven years and argues that Corbin’s inability to locate 35 of 47 CoCs within that retention period is unjustified and warrants compelled discovery and a sworn declaration.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Raises spoliation concern regarding missing CoCs
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly connects the 35 missing CoCs to Corbin's seven-year retention obligation, requests retention/destruction policies and litigation hold information, discusses whether the CoCs were lost or destroyed after a duty to preserve arose, cites spoliation authority and Rule 37(e), and reserves the right to seek Rule 37(e) sanctions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Requests sworn declaration on search methodology
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly requests an order requiring Corbin to provide a sworn declaration regarding its search for the missing CoCs, retention practices, and litigation hold. The proposed order also requires a sworn declaration describing custodians, locations, systems searched, search methods, and disposition of missing Certificates of Conformance.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Challenges third-party confidentiality objection to RFP No. 37
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly addresses RFP No. 37 concerning Corbin–AMT communications, identifies Corbin’s objection based on AMT/third-party confidentiality, and argues that third-party confidentiality is not a privilege or valid basis to withhold documents under Rule 34, with any concerns addressable by protective order.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Argues protective order can address confidentiality
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues that third-party confidentiality is not a basis to withhold discovery and that any legitimate confidentiality interests, including AMT’s, can be addressed through the protective order Vantage offered or confidentiality designations rather than refusal to produce.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Argues document retention policy (RFP No. 31) is relevant
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues that RFP No. 31 seeking retention/destruction policies and litigation hold information is relevant because Corbin produced only 12 of 47 CoCs, claims the remaining 35 cannot be located despite contractual retention obligations, and those CoCs are central to the false certification/concealment allegations. It also requests production and a sworn declaration regarding the missing CoCs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Requests attorney's fees under Rule 37(a)(5)
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly requests an award of reasonable expenses, including attorney's fees, incurred in making the motion, and cites Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(a)(5)(A) in the Wherefore clause, memorandum, and proposed order.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Includes meet-and-confer certification
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion includes a dedicated “LOCAL RULE 37.1 CERTIFICATION OF GOOD-FAITH CONFERRAL” section certifying that counsel conferred in good faith, listing dates, participants, issues discussed, positions, and stating the disputes remain unresolved.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Certification references specific meet-and-confer dates
criteria_results.reasoning: The meet-and-confer certification expressly lists all four required dates: August 14, 2024 deficiency letter, August 28, 2024 telephone conference, September 9, 2024 follow-up letter, and October 7, 2024 final letter. The supporting narrative also references these dates.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Includes summary chart per Magistrate Judge standing order
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes Appendix A titled “SUMMARY CHART OF DISPUTED DISCOVERY REQUESTS,” expressly submitted pursuant to the Magistrate Judge’s standing order. The chart covers interrogatories and RFPs and, for each disputed item, identifies the request/interrogatory, Corbin’s objection or non-response, and Vantage’s position explaining why the objection should be overruled or production compelled.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Challenges 'millions of pages' burden claim as unsupported
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically challenges Corbin’s RFP No. 5 “millions of pages” burden claim as unsupported and facially implausible. It notes there is no declaration or cost estimate, and emphasizes the limited scope: one customer, one part family/specification, 47 purchase orders, approximately 4,280 units, and a 33-month shipment period. Appendix A repeats that the request is limited and that no burden evidence was provided.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Notes lack of supporting declaration/affidavit for burden claim
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues that Corbin’s burden objections are unsupported by evidence, including stating that Corbin provided “no declaration, no estimate of cost,” “no burden evidence,” and that objections were unsupported by any declaration quantifying burden.

criteria_results.title: Addresses Interrogatory No. 7 deficiency
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically addresses Interrogatory No. 7 multiple times, including in the argument section and Appendix A. It identifies Interrogatory No. 7 as seeking all QC testing on shipped components, notes Corbin objected without a substantive answer, explains why the information is core liability discovery, and requests an order compelling a full answer or proper Rule 33(d) specification.

criteria_results.title: Addresses Interrogatory No. 12 deficiency
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically addresses Interrogatory No. 12 in the memorandum and Appendix A, identifying it as seeking internal communications regarding quality issues, complaints, shipping non-passing parts, and investigations, describing Corbin’s objections/non-response, and arguing why a substantive response should be compelled.

criteria_results.title: Addresses RFP No. 14 deficiency
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically addresses RFP No. 14, identifying it as seeking electronic communications between QC and production departments regarding Vantage, components, VES-4400, CoCs, and quality issues, and argues that Corbin improperly refused production based on privilege, overbreadth, burden, and proportionality objections. It also seeks an order compelling production.

criteria_results.title: Cites Rule 26(b)(1) scope of discovery
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum's Legal Standard expressly cites Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(1) and quotes the scope of discovery as nonprivileged matter relevant to any party's claim or defense and proportional to the needs of the case.

criteria_results.title: Requests order compelling responses within specified time
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly requests an order compelling Corbin, within fourteen (14) days, to serve complete verified answers to Interrogatory Nos. 1–25 and complete written responses and production for Request Nos. 1–42. The proposed order repeats the 14-day compliance deadline.

criteria_results.title: Includes proposed order
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes a separate section titled “[PROPOSED] ORDER GRANTING PLAINTIFF'S MOTION TO COMPEL DISCOVERY RESPONSES,” which grants the motion and sets out the requested relief, including compelling responses, addressing privilege waiver, confidentiality, retention policies, fees, and sanctions.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states total damages claimed as $14.7 million
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion states that Vantage alleges damages exceeding $14.7 million and later references the amount in controversy as exceeding $14.7 million. This correctly reflects the required $14.7 million total damages figure and does not materially misstate it.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states number of failed turbine units as 38
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion states that there were “thirty-eight turbine failures” and later refers to “the 38 failed units,” matching the required number of 38.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states total units shipped as 4,280 across 47 POs
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion correctly states that Corbin shipped approximately 4,280 turbine housings and repeatedly references 47 purchase orders, including “~4,280 units, ~47 POs” and related statements such as 35 of 47 CoCs missing.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies Foss email date as September 14, 2022
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly identifies the Gerald Foss email as dated September 14, 2022, including in the motion, memorandum, certification, appendix, and exhibit index.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states 15 housings in Foss email batch
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly states that the Foss email reported a batch of 15 housings that did not pass CMM inspection and were cleared for shipment. No different number is used for that email batch.

criteria_results.title: DISTRACTOR_003: Does not overstate production as total stonewalling
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly acknowledges that Corbin served responses and produced an initial 312-page production, including the MSA, purchase-order confirmations, invoice summaries, organizational chart, insurance declaration pages, financial information, twelve CoCs, and the Foss email. Although it argues the production was grossly inadequate and that Corbin refused to produce core categories of documents, it does not claim Corbin produced zero documents or completely refused to participate in discovery.

criteria_results.title: References Local Rule 37.1 by name or number
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly cites “Local Rule 37.1” in the opening paragraph and includes a “LOCAL RULE 37.1 CERTIFICATION OF GOOD-FAITH CONFERRAL.”

criteria_results.title: References Magistrate Judge Sheehan's standing order
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly cites “Magistrate Judge Sheehan's Standing Order Regarding Discovery Motions” and states that the Summary Chart is attached as required by the Standing Order, with Appendix A labeled as submitted pursuant to that order.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum of law is included or incorporated
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes a separate section titled “PLAINTIFF VANTAGE INDUSTRIAL HOLDINGS, INC.'S MEMORANDUM OF LAW IN SUPPORT OF ITS MOTION TO COMPEL DISCOVERY RESPONSES,” with a legal standard, argument sections, case citations, rule analysis, and application to the discovery disputes.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies discovery served on June 17, 2024
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly states that Vantage served its First Set of Interrogatories and First Request for Production of Documents on June 17, 2024, which matches the required date.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states responses served on July 31, 2024
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly states that Corbin served its responses and objections on July 31, 2024, including in the motion, factual background, and exhibit index. No different response date is stated.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Corbin's response statistics for interrogatories
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion discusses interrogatory deficiencies and lists many individual issues, but it does not state or substantially convey the required statistical breakdown that, out of 25 interrogatories, Corbin provided substantive answers to only 8, objected to 14 without substantive response, and gave partial/evasive answers to 3. Its summary instead refers generally to a “handful” of corresponding responses and identifies different categories without the specified counts.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Corbin's response statistics for RFPs
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion discusses Corbin’s RFP responses and includes an itemized chart, but it does not state or substantially summarize the required breakdown that, out of 42 RFPs, Corbin objected to 29 in their entirety and provided only partial production for 13.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies 12 of 47 CoCs produced
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly states that Corbin produced only 12 Certificates of Conformance out of 47, and that 35 of 47 are missing. Neither number is materially misstated.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Allegheny Materials Testing by name
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly identifies Allegheny Materials Testing, Inc. (“AMT”) as Corbin’s metallurgical testing subcontractor and specifically discusses Corbin–AMT communications in connection with RFP No. 37.

criteria_results.title: References Bates stamp or production identification for Foss email
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly identifies the Foss email by its Bates number, including references to “CORBIN-000247,” and describes it as part of Corbin’s production.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies MSA execution date as March 15, 2021
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion states that the Master Supply Agreement was dated March 15, 2021, including in the opening paragraph and exhibit index. It does not state a different MSA execution date.

criteria_results.title: Addresses RFP No. 22 specifically regarding CoCs
criteria_results.reasoning: The output specifically identifies RFP 22/Request No. 22 as seeking Certificates of Conformance for each shipment and addresses Corbin’s deficient response, including that only 12 CoCs were produced and 35 could not be located despite retention obligations.

criteria_results.title: Addresses RFP No. 31 specifically regarding retention policies
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically identifies RFP/Request No. 31 as seeking retention/destruction policies and litigation hold notices, and it directly challenges Corbin’s relevance objection as untenable given the missing CoCs and retention obligations.

criteria_results.title: Addresses RFP No. 37 specifically regarding Allegheny communications
criteria_results.reasoning: The output specifically identifies RFP 37 as seeking Corbin--AMT (Allegheny Materials Testing) communications regarding Type 347 testing and expressly challenges Corbin's AMT/third-party confidentiality objection as not a privilege and addressable by protective order.

criteria_results.title: Fact discovery deadline correctly stated as March 31, 2025
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion mentions the fact discovery deadline as closing on March 31, 2025, which matches the required date, and does not state a conflicting fact discovery deadline.

criteria_results.title: Correctly attributes evasive Interrogatory 18 response language
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly quotes Corbin’s Interrogatory No. 18 response as stating it is “not aware of any parts that ‘failed’ internal quality inspection and were thereafter shipped to Vantage,” which matches the required language and does not change its meaning.
